questions.question: Which of the following statements about how flowering plants reproduce is correct?
options: Flowering plants reproduce sexually.
Flowering plants reproduce only through binary fission.
Flowering plants reproduce only through budding.
Flowering plants do not reproduce and rely on spores.

questions.question: What are the female gametes in flowering plants called?
options: Pollen grains
Anthers
Egg cells (ova)
Zygotes

questions.question: Which part of a flowering plant carries the male gametes?
options: Ovary
Pollen grains
Stigma
Petals

questions.question: What are the three main components that make up a seed, which is formed in the ovary?
options: An embryo, food store and a tough outer coat
Pollen grain, a zygote and a stem
A leaf, root and flower bud
Nectar, petals and anthers

questions.question: What is a fruit, biologically speaking, in a seed-producing plant?
options: The swollen stem supporting the flower
The mature and ripened ovary
The collection of petals after pollination
The pollen tube that has hardened

questions.question: What is the primary role of a pollinator in plant reproduction?
options: To disperse seeds away from the parent plant
To carry water to the roots of the flower
To transfer pollen from one flower to another
To consume pests that eat the plant's leaves

questions.question: Which group makes up the majority of pollinators, with bees being the largest group within it?
options: Birds
Mammals
Insects
Reptiles

questions.question: What is meant by the term 'food security'?
options: Protecting agricultural fields with high fences and security guards
Ensuring that food is heavily processed to prevent spoilage
Having enough affordable and nutritious food in an area or country
Storing seeds in underground bunkers for future centuries

questions.question: What is pollination?
options: The fusion of male and female sex cells
The growth of a pollen tube down the style
The transfer of pollen from the male anther to the female stigma
The release of seeds from a mature fruit

questions.question: What is a key benefit of cross-pollination compared to self-pollination?
options: It requires no pollinators whatsoever
It increases variation in a species
It makes the plant grow seeds much faster
It uses much less pollen

questions.question: Which of the following describes the process of fertilisation in plants?
options: The movement of pollen by insects from flower to flower
The fusion of the nuclei from the male and female gametes
The growth of a seed on a wet cotton wool substrate
The dispersal of seeds away from the parent plant by wind

questions.question: When analysing experimental data from a plant investigation, when should you use a line graph instead of a bar chart?
options: When the independent variable is categoric
When you want to display the names of different seed types
When the independent variable is continuous
When there are no numerical values recorded

questions.question: How are wind-dispersed seeds adapted to their method of dispersal?
options: They are heavy with a sticky outer surface to cling to objects
They are enclosed in juicy, bright fruits to attract birds
They are light with a large surface area
They have hooks that latch onto animal fur

questions.question: Which material is commonly used in school laboratories to demonstrate that some seeds, like cress, can germinate under the right conditions without soil?
options: Sterile sand
Cotton wool
Crushed gravel
Dry plastic beads

questions.question: In an investigation measuring how far model seeds disperse, what is the dependent variable?
options: The starting height from which the seed is dropped
The type of paper used to make the model seed
The distance the seed travels
The speed of the wind from the fan

questions.question: Why is it important to repeat measurements for each value in a seed dispersal or germination investigation?
options: To change the independent variable halfway through the experiment
To identify anomalous results and calculate a mean
To ensure the seeds grow into different plant species
To reduce the amount of equipment needed
